subject: Computer Networking
title: TCP/IP: The Universal Language
description: One-minute skill: TCP/IP: The Universal Language.

hook.text: Different networks existed by the 1970s — but none could talk to each other. Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn fixed that.

buildup.text: They designed TCP/IP to work across any network type — wired, wireless, satellite. A universal protocol suite.

discovery.text: TCP handles reliable delivery. IP handles addressing and routing. Together they connect anything to anything.

twist.text: On January 1, 1983 — Flag Day — ARPANET switched from NCP to TCP/IP. Every host had to upgrade at once.

climax.text: That single switch unified networking forever. TCP/IP is still the foundation of the internet today.

punchline.text: TCP/IP didn't just connect networks. It became the internet.

quiz.question: When did ARPANET officially switch from NCP to TCP/IP?

details.summary: TCP/IP, designed by Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn in the 1970s, became the universal protocol suite for internetworking. TCP ensures reliable data delivery while IP handles addressing and routing across diverse networks.
details.whyItMatters: TCP/IP is the protocol that makes the internet possible. It allows any type of network to connect to any other, creating one unified global system from millions of diverse networks.
takeaways: TCP handles reliable delivery; IP handles addressing and routing
TCP/IP replaced NCP on ARPANET in January 1983
It enables diverse networks to interconnect seamlessly

faq.question: What made TCP/IP better than previous protocols?
faq.answer: TCP/IP separated reliability from routing, allowing it to work across any type of network. NCP assumed a single reliable network. TCP/IP made each endpoint responsible for reliability, so it worked even when crossing unreliable or different network types.

faq.question: Why is TCP/IP still used after 40 plus years?
faq.answer: Its layered design is elegant and flexible. IP handles routing without caring about content. TCP handles reliability without caring about the path. This separation means new technologies can replace either layer without affecting the other. IPv6 upgrades IP while keeping TCP.
